solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Everyone attending is not out to lunch

parts.note: everyone means all
attending means present, there

explanation.surface: Someone notes that the whole staff is present, so nobody has gone off for a midday meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out to lunch' is slang for crazy, so the definition means being of sound mind.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone with all faculties intact is sane, the opposite of the slang 'out to lunch' (mad).

clue.text: Bill and Paul excitedly combined operations in holiday venue

parts.note: AC is an abbreviation for account, a bill

indicators.note: excitedly suggests something stirred up and jumbled

parts.note: CO is the military abbreviation for Combined Operations

explanation.surface: Two men, Bill and Paul, eagerly join forces in a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name beside Paul, but it is AC (account).
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Mexican Pacific resort is a well-known place for vacations.

clue.text: Not entirely relaxed about King's appearance

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shortened word goes around the other piece
not entirely means the last letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: relaxed means loose
K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

explanation.surface: A monarch's demeanour seems a little tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a person's looks are their outward appearance.

clue.text: Hurrying to secure European trial

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast, so one piece is held within the other

parts.note: haring means rushing like a hare, hurrying

explanation.surface: Rushing to lock in a test run on the continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a court hearing is a judicial trial or examination of a case.

clue.text: Log mostly rolled over in attack

indicators.note: rolled over in a down clue means the letters are turned upside down, read in reverse
mostly means all but the final letter

parts.note: a log or record is a diary

explanation.surface: A tree trunk tumbles over during an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts DIARY to DIAR, which 'rolled over' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a raid is a sudden assault.

clue.text: Funny programme — it has company engaged in S&M

indicators.note: engaged in means occupied within, so these pieces go inside the outer letters

parts.note: S&M is written down as its two letters S and M

explanation.surface: A cheeky description of a comedy show involving a firm mixed up in sadomasochism.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation comedy is a kind of light-hearted broadcast series, a funny programme.

clue.text: I am heroic without hesitation, being misrepresented as theatrical villain

indicators.note: misrepresented suggests the letters are shown in a false arrangement
without means lacking, so these letters are taken away

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A boastful claim of heroism, made without faltering, turns out to be a lie about a stage baddie.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing ER leaves IAMHOIC, which 'being misrepresented' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: the scheming Italian in Shakespeare's Cymbeline is a stage villain.

clue.text: Items of armour required — I'll be beset by scoundrel and fools

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so this piece sits inside the next

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible man, a scoundrel
I'll is read as I will, giving the letter I
asses are fools

explanation.surface: A knight needs protective gear, fearing attack from a rogue and idiots.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: breastplates covering the torso are pieces of armour.

clue.text: French artist capturing girl's foremost source of attraction

indicators.note: capturing means holding within, so the outer piece surrounds the inner

parts.note: Manet was a French painter

indicators.note: foremost means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A French painter catches a girl's chief appeal on canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal and figurative: a magnet draws iron to it, and something that draws people is likewise a pull.

clue.text: Business share prompting a lot of admiration

parts.note: business in the sense of fuss or bother is ado
a share or allotted portion is a ration

explanation.surface: A company's stock allocation is drawing plenty of praise from investors.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: adoration is intense love or worship, a great deal of admiration.

clue.text: Old storm at sea appearing in no novel

indicators.note: appearing in means showing up inside, so these letters go within the outer word
at sea means confused, so the letters of the word are jumbled

explanation.surface: An ancient tempest on the ocean fails to feature in any book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like 'new', but is the definition: Conrad's book.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Joseph Conrad's 1904 tale of a South American port is a work of fiction.

clue.text: Hold on — just over 50% recycling?

indicators.note: just over half of a nine-letter word is its final five letters, the portion taken here

explanation.surface: Someone queries whether recycling rates have only just passed the halfway mark, asking us to wait a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to keep a tight grip on something, refusing to let go.

clue.text: Happy, it would seem, to include one not mentioned

indicators.note: to include means to hold within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: happy is jokingly read as not sad, written as one word un-sad
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A cheerful person seems to bring along someone who never got a mention.
explanation.walkthrough: UNSAD is not a real word: 'it would seem' warns that 'happy' is being rendered literally as 'not sad'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something left unspoken has gone unmentioned.

clue.text: Guess I'm tucking into what's left

indicators.note: tucking into means slipping inside, so these letters go within the other piece

parts.note: what someone leaves at death is their estate
taken as its letters, I and M

explanation.surface: Someone guesses while eating up the leftovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' suggests eating, but it signals insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a guess is a rough judgement, an estimate.

clue.text: A dubious action involving masseur's beginning on bodily form

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other
dubious means suspect, signalling the letters are rearranged
beginning means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A questionable act by a masseur, starting on someone's body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dubious' makes NATOIC from ACTION, which takes in M.
explanation.definitionFit: Relation: an adjective meaning concerning the structure of the body, so about bodily form.

clue.text: College, to keep going, prepares facilities for sportsmen

parts.note: to hang in is to persevere, keep going
grooms means prepares, as in readying someone for a role

explanation.surface: A college that refuses to give up gets the sports amenities ready.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: rooms where players change kit are amenities provided for those playing sport.

clue.text: Modern stadium, one subsequently occupied by part of London university

parts.note: one is the single article A

indicators.note: occupied by means filled by, so the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: subsequently means later
LSE, the London School of Economics, is a college of the University of London

explanation.surface: A new sports ground later taken over by a London college.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: since the 1990s, top British football grounds have had to provide seating for every fan, unlike old terraced stadiums.

clue.text: Cook coating each article with a light touch

indicators.note: coating means covering, so the outer word surrounds the others

parts.note: to fry is to cook
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A chef glazes each item delicately.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative: something like a plume is light and soft, so delicate in touch.

clue.text: Greeting that could make someone tingle

indicators.note: could make suggests the letters can be fashioned into something new

explanation.surface: A welcome so warm it sends a shiver through someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: this informal phrase is said on meeting someone after a long absence, so it is a greeting.

clue.text: Is nothing in American city unpleasant?

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so these letters go within the city name

parts.note: Nome is a city in Alaska
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A question asking whether a US city has nothing nasty about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: noisome means offensive or disgusting, especially in smell.

clue.text: Routine number of performances kept up by comedienne's latest feed

indicators.note: kept up in a down clue means held upside down, the letters read in reverse

parts.note: a rut is a dull routine
a show's run is its series of performances

indicators.note: latest means the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A comic's long-running act is sustained by her newest material.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to nurture is to nourish or feed and raise.

clue.text: Special work for newspaper? Hurry

parts.note: to print is what a press does for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A rush job for the press, with a deadline looming.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to sprint is to run fast, to hurry.

clue.text: Regular payments before parents may import one

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before

indicators.note: import means bring in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: mums are mothers, parents
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Instalments paid ahead of time, which parents might bring in from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: insurance premiums are recurring sums paid to keep cover in force.

clue.text: Tense tirade about University student declining to study

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: a tirade is a rant

explanation.surface: A strained outburst over a university pupil refusing to work.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: a pupil who skips school without leave is choosing not to study.

clue.text: Separate aim of an audition?

definitions.meaning: an actor auditions hoping to win a role in a play

explanation.surface: An actor wonders what the point of trying out alone is.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: as one word it means asunder; split as two words it is a role, which auditioning seeks.

clue.text: Expecting to receive endless data

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: to be in for something is to be due to get it, as in 'in for a shock'

explanation.surface: Someone awaits a never-ending stream of figures.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbreviation: info is short for information, which is data.

clue.text: Start occupying 21 rooms

indicators.note: occupying means filling the space within, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: 21 stands for the solution to 21 Down, a word for a dash, followed by the word rooms as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to begin by taking over a number of rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: '21' stands for the answer to 21 Down, SPRINT; the answer sits across the end of it and the start of 'rooms'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an introduction is the opening or start of a piece.

clue.text: Get opinion of European about a foreign embassy

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: to get someone's opinion is to consult them

explanation.surface: A traveller seeks a European's view on an overseas mission.
explanation.definitionFit: Near-synonym: a consulate is a diplomatic office of a foreign state, much like an embassy.

clue.text: Sailor to achieve aim

parts.note: tar is an old slang word for a sailor
to get something is to achieve or obtain it

explanation.surface: A seaman sets out to reach a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an aim or goal is a target.

clue.text: Rural activity supporting economy, ultimately involving others

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: supporting means in favour of, for
the others means the rest

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A country pursuit that props up the local economy, which in the end draws in other people.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the management of woodland is a countryside occupation.
